title: ‘1619,’ Episode 4: How the Bad Blood Started

sentences.en: My Uncle Eddie was my favorite uncle.
sentences.zh: 埃迪叔叔是我最喜欢的叔叔。

sentences.en: He was my dad's younger brother, not that much older than me, and he was a complete jokester and cut up.
sentences.zh: 他是我爸爸的弟弟，年纪比我大不了多少，是个十足的乐天派和开心果。

sentences.en: He was the one who was always playing some practical joke on you or who in some ways always felt was taking things too far because he just thought everything was funny.
sentences.zh: 他总是喜欢搞些恶作剧，有时我觉得他有点过火，因为他觉得什么都好笑。

sentences.en: So, for instance, if you fell asleep in his house, he might light a match and stick it between your toes and let it burn down to wake you because he thought it was funny.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你在他家睡着了，他可能会点燃一根火柴，插在你的脚趾缝里，让它烧到尽头把你烫醒，因为他觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: He called me Bird, which was my nickname, and we liked to listen to music together.
sentences.zh: 他叫我“小鸟”，这是我的昵称，我们喜欢一起听音乐。

sentences.en: We liked to watch TV together.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢一起看电视。

sentences.en: He was never mad.
sentences.zh: 他从不生气。

sentences.en: I never remember him ever disciplining me for anything.
sentences.zh: 我不记得他曾因为任何事责罚过我。

sentences.en: And, in fact, when my father and I would fight when I was a teenager, I would sometimes pack my bag and go stay with him for a couple of days,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我十几岁和父亲吵架时，我有时会收拾行李去他那里住上几天，

sentences.en: and he would never kind of sell me out.
sentences.zh: 他从来不会出卖我。

sentences.en: When I got into college at the University of Notre Dame, I think the only person prouder than my mom and dad was my Uncle Ed.
sentences.zh: 当我考上圣母大学时，我想除了我父母之外，最骄傲的人就是埃迪叔叔了。

sentences.en: And when I graduated, my uncle picked out this all-red outfit from head to toe.
sentences.zh: 我毕业时，叔叔特意挑选了一套从头到脚全红的行头。

sentences.en: He had on a red hat and a red shirt and red pants and these red gaiters,
sentences.zh: 他戴着红帽子，穿着红衬衫、红裤子，还戴着红护腿，

sentences.en: and he was determined that he was going to show everyone how proud he was of me by outdressing everyone at the graduation.
sentences.zh: 他下定决心要在毕业典礼上穿得比谁都显眼，以此向大家展示他为我感到多么骄傲。

sentences.en: And he certainly did.
sentences.zh: 他确实做到了。

sentences.en: So we just were always very close.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直非常亲近。

sentences.en: Whenever I would come home, we would get breakfast together at morgues and just talk about life.
sentences.zh: 每当我回家，我们都会一起去吃早餐，聊聊生活。

sentences.en: And all he would tell me all the time was how proud he was of me.
sentences.zh: 他总是不断地告诉我他为我感到多么骄傲。

sentences.en: Besides being a lot of fun, my Uncle Ed was also one of the hardest-working men that I knew.
sentences.zh: 埃迪叔叔不仅风趣幽默，还是我认识的最勤劳的人之一。

sentences.en: He worked a lot of jobs doing things like working in animal processing plants.
sentences.zh: 他做过很多工作，比如在肉类加工厂上班。

sentences.en: And the last job that he had was roofing, and he did roofing for a lot of years,
sentences.zh: 他最后一份工作是做屋顶维修，他干了很多年，

sentences.en: often coming home at the end of the day kind of grimy and sometimes with his joints in his hands so swollen that he couldn't even make a fiSt.
sentences.zh: 每天下班回家时总是灰头土脸，有时手关节肿得连拳头都握不住。

sentences.en: He relished working hard.
sentences.zh: 他以辛勤工作为荣。

sentences.en: He was proud that he could provide for his family even without an education.
sentences.zh: 他为自己即使没有受过教育也能养活家人而感到自豪。

sentences.en: And then about 2009, he started to feel a pretty severe pain in his back, and that pain began to spread from his back down into his legs, and he started to have trouble moving.
sentences.zh: 大约在2009年，他开始感到背部剧痛，疼痛从背部蔓延到腿部，行动开始变得困难。

sentences.en: And there were some mornings where he would have to kind of crawl out of bed.
sentences.zh: 有些早晨，他甚至得爬着下床。

sentences.en: But around that time, my Uncle also got laid off from the job where he was doing roofing.
sentences.zh: 但就在那时，叔叔也因为做屋顶维修的工作被解雇了。

sentences.en: And with that layoff, he lost his health insurance.
sentences.zh: 随着失业，他失去了医疗保险。

sentences.en: So, like many people, he at first avoided going to the doctor altogether because he didn't have insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以，像许多人一样，他起初因为没有保险而完全不去医院看病。

sentences.en: But then when it got kind of unbearable, he went to the free clinic.
sentences.zh: 但后来疼痛变得难以忍受，他去了免费诊所。

sentences.en: Because my Uncle did not have health insurance, they would not give him the test that he probably needed to find out what was going on with his back.
sentences.zh: 因为叔叔没有医疗保险，他们不肯给他做检查，而他本需要这些检查来查明背部的问题。

sentences.en: They wouldn't give him an X-ray, they wouldn't give him a CAT scan or a PET scan.
sentences.zh: 他们不给他拍X光片，也不给他做CT或PET扫描。

sentences.en: And instead, they just tried to diagnose based on what he was telling them.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们只是根据他的描述试图进行诊断。

sentences.en: And they told him that he probably just needed an alignment in his spine, that that's what was bothering his back.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉他，他可能只是需要矫正一下脊椎，说这就是他背痛的原因。

sentences.en: So they sent him to a chiropractor.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把他转介给了脊椎按摩师。

sentences.en: My Uncle would end up going back about five or six times as his back was getting progressively worse.
sentences.zh: 随着背部状况日益恶化，叔叔最终去了五六次。

sentences.en: And the final time that he went to the chiropractor, as the doctor was working on his back, they both heard a big pop.
sentences.zh: 最后一次去按摩师那里时，医生在给他治疗背部时，两人都听到了一声巨响。

sentences.en: That pop concerned everyone.
sentences.zh: 那声响让所有人都担心起来。

sentences.en: And so the chiropractor told him, as my Uncle kind of gets up off the bed and is barely able to stand up, that he better go to the emergency room right away.
sentences.zh: 于是，当叔叔从床上艰难地爬起来，几乎站不稳时，按摩师告诉他最好立刻去急诊室。

sentences.en: When he got to the emergency room,
sentences.zh: 当他到达急诊室时，

sentences.en: that doctor recognized right away that something serious was going on and actually gave my uncle the X-ray and the CAT scan that he probably had needed months before.
sentences.zh: 医生立刻意识到情况严重，并给叔叔做了他几个月前就该做的X光和CT扫描。

sentences.en: And what that doctor saw scared him.
sentences.zh: 医生看到的结果让他感到害怕。

sentences.en: He saw these spots on the scans that he had taken all over my uncle's back and along his spine.
sentences.zh: 他在扫描片上看到叔叔的背部和脊椎上到处都是斑点。

sentences.en: And it's at that point where we find out that my uncle has cancer and that he'd likely had cancer for many, many months, if not longer.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我们得知叔叔患了癌症，而且很可能已经患病好几个月，甚至更久了。

sentences.en: And we learned that the cancer is stage four and it has metastasized throughout its entire body.
sentences.zh: 我们得知癌症已是四期，并且已经扩散到全身。

sentences.en: And because of that, the cancer is terminal.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，这是绝症。

sentences.en: And it is because of that diagnosis that my uncle was finally able to get access to the insurance that he had needed so badly all those months before.
sentences.zh: 也正是因为这个诊断，叔叔终于获得了他几个月前急需的保险。

sentences.en: And that's because with this diagnosis of terminal untreatable cancer, my uncle was able to qualify for federal disability.
sentences.zh: 因为有了这种绝症诊断，叔叔才有资格申请联邦残疾补助。

sentences.en: And federal disability means because your physical health is so poor and you are unable to work, the government will help you and pay for your insurance and your medical treatment.
sentences.zh: 联邦残疾补助意味着，由于你的身体状况太差无法工作，政府会帮助你并支付你的保险和医疗费用。

sentences.en: So it took literally my uncle getting a death sentence before he was able to get health insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以，叔叔实际上是拿到了死亡判决书，才终于得到了医疗保险。

sentences.en: That health care gets him out of those free clinics and into an actual cancer clinic in Illinois.
sentences.zh: 那份医疗保障让他离开了免费诊所，进入了伊利诺伊州的一家正规癌症诊所。

sentences.en: And it's there that the doctors give us the news that had they been able to see him months before, he could have had a fighting chance.
sentences.zh: 在那里，医生告诉我们，如果他们能早几个月看到他，他本还有一线生机。

sentences.en: But it was too late.
sentences.zh: 但一切都太晚了。

sentences.en: And so in those next four months, we just saw my uncle's health deteriorate more rapidly than any of us could have imagined.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的四个月里，我们眼睁睁地看着叔叔的健康状况恶化得比我们想象的还要快。

sentences.en: And his body withered to almost nothing.
sentences.zh: 他的身体消瘦得几乎只剩皮包骨。

sentences.en: And in the end, the pain of the cancer was so bad that he didn't even want to fight anymore.
sentences.zh: 最后，癌症带来的痛苦太剧烈了，他甚至不想再抗争了。

sentences.en: So at the age of 50, just two weeks after my daughter was born, my uncle passed away.
sentences.zh: 于是，在50岁那年，就在我女儿出生两周后，叔叔去世了。

sentences.en: I remember in those last days when he was in hospice and I had just had my baby, I called him to give him the news.
sentences.zh: 我记得在他临终前，他住在临终关怀医院，我刚生完孩子，打电话告诉他这个消息。

sentences.en: He was really weak.
sentences.zh: 他非常虚弱。

sentences.en: He could barely talk.
sentences.zh: 几乎说不出话来。

sentences.en: But he said, I'm so happy that I'm going to get to see my baby bird.
sentences.zh: 但他还是说：“我真高兴能见到我的小鸟宝宝。”

sentences.en: And so when my daughter was just two weeks old, I had to wrap her up and put her on an airplane as we flew back to Waterloo to bury my uncle.
sentences.zh: 所以，当女儿才两周大时，我不得不把她裹好带上飞机，飞回滑铁卢去安葬叔叔。

sentences.en: From the New York Times Magazine, I'm Nicole Hannah-Jones.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的妮可·汉娜-琼斯。

sentences.en: This is 1619.
Okay, Janine Interlandi, where do you want to start?
sentences.zh: 好的，珍妮·因特兰迪，你想从哪里开始？

sentences.en: I think we should start in the fall of 1866 with a woman named Rebecca Lee Crumpler.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该从1866年秋天说起，主角是一位名叫丽贝卡·李·克伦普勒的女性。

sentences.en: Rebecca Lee Crumpler is a young Black woman who was born free and raised in Pennsylvania by her aunt.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡·李·克伦普勒是一位年轻的黑人女性，她生来自由，由姑姑在宾夕法尼亚州抚养长大。

sentences.en: Her aunt was a medicine woman.
sentences.zh: 她的姑姑是一位民间医生。

sentences.en: She used to go from home to home tending to the sick, and Rebecca liked to tag along and to help her.
sentences.zh: 她经常挨家挨户照顾病人，丽贝卡喜欢跟着她去帮忙。

sentences.en: She liked it so much that she went on to become a nurse.
sentences.zh: 她非常喜欢这份工作，后来成为了一名护士。

sentences.en: And she was so good at being a nurse that she makes the really unusual decision to go on and become a doctor.
sentences.zh: 她护士做得非常出色，以至于她做出了一个非常不寻常的决定：继续深造成为一名医生。

sentences.en: So she eventually goes to the New England Female Medical College, which is a college that was specifically built to train women in medicine.
sentences.zh: 于是她最终进入了新英格兰女性医学院，这是一所专门为女性提供医学培训的学院。

sentences.en: And that's really extraordinary, because around the time she graduates, there's about 54,000 doctors in the country, and only 300 of them are women.
sentences.zh: 这非常了不起，因为在她毕业时，全国大约有54,000名医生，其中只有300名是女性。

sentences.en: And only one of those women is Black.
sentences.zh: 而这其中只有一名是黑人女性。

sentences.en: And that woman is Rebecca Lee Crumpler.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是丽贝卡·李·克伦普勒。

sentences.en: And so about a year after she finishes medical school, the Civil War comes to an end.
sentences.zh: 在她医学院毕业大约一年后，内战结束了。

sentences.en: And she makes another unusual decision, which is to completely uproot her life and to head down to the cell.
sentences.zh: 她又做出了另一个不同寻常的决定，那就是彻底离开原来的生活，前往南方。

sentences.en: Do you remember when the Civil War was being followed?
sentences.zh: 你还记得内战是怎么被关注的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I can't remember much about it, but I remember this much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记不太清了，但我记得这么多。

sentences.en: Because 4 million people have just been released from slavery into freedom.
sentences.zh: 因为有400万人刚刚从奴隶制中获得自由。

sentences.en: And I thought old Marshall was dead, but he had been off to the wall and come back.
sentences.zh: 我以为老马歇尔死了，但他去打仗又回来了。

sentences.en: And old Marshall didn't tell you no it was free.
sentences.zh: 老马歇尔没告诉你自由了。

sentences.en: He didn't tell you that?
sentences.zh: 他没告诉你？

sentences.en: No, he didn't tell you.
sentences.zh: 没有，他没告诉你。

sentences.en: And Crumpler knows that it's going to be a huge challenge to help these people assimilate into society and to address their many basic needs, including health care.
sentences.zh: 克伦普勒知道，帮助这些人融入社会并解决他们许多基本需求（包括医疗保健）将是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: I said, Mama, where are they going?
sentences.zh: 我说，妈妈，他们要去哪儿？

sentences.en: They said, well, all of you niggas is all free now.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，你们这些黑鬼现在都自由了。

sentences.en: Yank is all going home.
sentences.zh: 北方佬都要回家了。

sentences.en: I spent a lot of time reading the slave narratives.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间阅读奴隶叙事。

sentences.en: And we're not really taught that emancipation came and someone would walk on the plantation and say, you are free.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有真正被教导说解放来临时，会有人走进种植园说：“你们自由了。”

sentences.en: But nothing came with that.
sentences.zh: 但随之而来的什么都没有。

sentences.en: These were people who just literally were told, you're free to go, but given no resources to go with.
sentences.zh: 这些人只是被告知“你们可以走了”，但没有给他们任何离开的资源。

sentences.en: Even just with basic shelter.
sentences.zh: 甚至连基本的住所都没有。

sentences.en: We didn't have no property.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何财产。

sentences.en: We didn't have no home.
sentences.zh: 我们没有家。

sentences.en: They didn't have places to go.
sentences.zh: 他们无处可去。

sentences.en: I was about 9, 10 years old, maybe anymore.
sentences.zh: 我当时大约9、10岁，可能再大一点。

sentences.en: Stayed right there.
sentences.zh: 就待在那里。

sentences.en: We didn't know where to go.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道该去哪儿。

sentences.en: We had nowhere.
sentences.zh: 我们无处可去。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: We didn't have nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们一无所有。

sentences.en: We just laid the cattle.
sentences.zh: 我们只能睡在牲口棚里。

sentences.en: We just turned out.
sentences.zh: 我们就像被赶出来一样。

sentences.en: So they were forced to take up residence in abandoned prisons, former military barracks, empty churches, refugee camps.
sentences.zh: 所以他们被迫住进废弃的监狱、旧军营、空教堂和难民营。

sentences.en: I remember one night I was out after I was free and I didn't have nowhere to go.
sentences.zh: 我记得有天晚上，我自由后在外面，无处可去。

sentences.en: I didn't have nowhere to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我没地方睡觉。

sentences.en: I didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: They're crammed together in very close living quarters.
sentences.zh: 他们挤在非常狭窄的居住空间里。

sentences.en: They don't have the tools necessary to maintain good hygiene.
sentences.zh: 他们没有保持良好卫生的必要工具。

sentences.en: And as a result of all of this, they're getting sick.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们都生病了。

sentences.en: But they can't tap into any health care system because at that time, there really isn't any organized health care system to speak of.
sentences.zh: 但他们无法利用任何医疗保健系统，因为当时根本没有所谓的有组织的医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: Most medical care is provided at home by family members or by doctors who would actually visit the house.
sentences.zh: 大多数医疗服务是由家庭成员在家中提供，或者由医生上门诊治。

sentences.en: And the only hospitals that exist are much more like institutions for the very poor or for people who get sick and don't have any family members to take care of them.
sentences.zh: 而当时仅有的医院更像是为极度贫困者，或是为那些生病了又没有家人照顾的人准备的机构。

sentences.en: And those facilities were private and they were run by charitable groups.
sentences.zh: 这些设施是私人的，由慈善团体运营。

sentences.en: And when the newly emancipated turned to those facilities for help, they were turned away.
sentences.zh: 当刚获得解放的人向这些机构寻求帮助时，他们被拒之门外。

sentences.en: They were told no.
sentences.zh: 他们被拒绝了。

sentences.en: And they start dying in really high numbers.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始大量死亡。

sentences.en: So much so that in some towns and cities, their bodies are littering the streets.
sentences.zh: 以至于在一些城镇，街上到处都是尸体。

sentences.en: This is a massive public health crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大的公共卫生危机。

sentences.en: And so to deal with this crisis, the federal government creates what ends up being the nation's first federal health care program.
sentences.zh: 为了应对这场危机，联邦政府创建了后来成为全国第一个联邦医疗保健计划的项目。

sentences.en: It's called the Freedmen's Bureau Medical Division.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“自由民局医疗部”。

sentences.en: And this is what Rebecca Crumpler is heading south to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是丽贝卡·克伦普勒前往南方要去做的事情。

sentences.en: She's going to Virginia to treat the newly emancipated through this new medical program.
sentences.zh: 她要去弗吉尼亚州，通过这个新的医疗项目来救治刚获得解放的人。

sentences.en: And what does she see when she gets there?
sentences.zh: 她到那里后看到了什么？

sentences.en: So when she gets to the south and she starts working, she sees that this new program is a complete mess.
sentences.zh: 当她到达南方开始工作时，她发现这个新项目简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: The hospitals she has gone to, just like all of the other hospitals in this program, are completely under-resourced.
sentences.zh: 她去的医院，就像这个项目中的所有其他医院一样，资源极度匮乏。

sentences.en: They don't have enough beds or sheets or linens.
sentences.zh: 他们没有足够的床位、床单或亚麻布。

sentences.en: They don't have enough medicine.
sentences.zh: 他们没有足够的药物。

sentences.en: They don't have enough quarantine facilities.
sentences.zh: 他们没有足够的隔离设施。

sentences.en: And they're in the middle of a smallpox outbreak.
sentences.zh: 而且当时正处于天花爆发期间。

sentences.en: And there's this horrible shortage of doctors.
sentences.zh: 医生严重短缺。

sentences.en: There's only about 120 doctors employed by the entire program.
sentences.zh: 整个项目雇佣的医生只有大约120名。

sentences.en: So you're saying that the federal government at that time was only supplying 100 doctors to serve the entire emancipated population of 4 million people?
sentences.zh: 你是说当时的联邦政府只提供了100名医生来服务400万刚获得解放的人口？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is one of the crazy things about the Freedmen's Bureau Medical Division, which is it was founded in utter ambivalence.
sentences.zh: 这就是自由民局医疗部最疯狂的地方之一，它是在极度的矛盾中建立的。

sentences.en: Officials wanted their communities clean enough to prevent diseases that might eventually spread into white communities.
sentences.zh: 官员们希望这些社区足够干净，以防止可能最终蔓延到白人社区的疾病。

sentences.en: But they don't want to provide any free assistance because they're worried that it's going to create dependency among the Black American community.
sentences.zh: 但他们又不想提供任何免费援助，因为他们担心这会在美国黑人社区中造成依赖性。

sentences.en: And so what they do is they open these hospitals and they staff them with a few doctors.
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的就是开设这些医院，并配备几名医生。

sentences.en: But then they close them down at the first sign of progress.
sentences.zh: 但一旦看到一点进展，他们就会立刻关闭医院。

sentences.en: And they refuse to send resources that their own doctors, including Crumpler, are requesting.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝提供包括克伦普勒在内的医生所请求的资源。

sentences.en: You know, they're saying, can we have additional staff to address the smallpox outbreak?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们问：“我们能增加人手来应对天花爆发吗？”

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: Can we have more blankets and more bedding?
sentences.zh: “我们能多要些毯子和床上用品吗？”

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: Can we have an extra facility for quarantine so that the diseases don't spread?
sentences.zh: “我们能多建一个隔离设施以防止疾病传播吗？”

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, Black people continue to die at very, very high rates.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，黑人的死亡率依然居高不下。

sentences.en: In that hospital in Virginia where Rebecca Crumpler has gone, what specifically is standing in the way of hospitals like that getting more support?
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚州丽贝卡·克伦普勒工作的医院里，究竟是什么阻碍了像这样的医院获得更多支持？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things was, as you have all of these people dying from preventable things, a theory emerges.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个原因是，当所有这些人死于可预防的疾病时，一种理论出现了。

sentences.en: And the theory goes that this high death rate is actually just nature taking its course.
sentences.zh: 理论上认为，这种高死亡率其实只是自然规律在起作用。

sentences.en: So Black people aren't dying for want of basic necessities.
sentences.zh: 所以黑人并不是因为缺乏基本生活必需品而死亡。

sentences.en: They're actually dying because they're biologically inferior to whites and ill-suited for freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们死亡是因为他们在生物学上不如白人，且不适合享有自由。

sentences.en: The argument became that African Americans specifically were literally going extinct and that to provide
sentences.zh: 当时的论点是，非裔美国人正在走向灭绝，如果提供

sentences.en: any type of funding or resources to fight that would be wasteful and foolish because you're just trying to prevent the inevitable.
sentences.zh: 任何形式的资金或资源来对抗这种趋势都是浪费和愚蠢的，因为你只是在试图阻止不可避免的事情发生。

sentences.en: And this theory actually gains pretty wide traction.
sentences.zh: 而这一理论实际上获得了相当广泛的支持。

sentences.en: There's a congressman from Ohio who uses it to argue against the freedmen's hospitals in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州的一位国会议员就利用这一理论来反对在美国建立自由民医院。

sentences.en: House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 众议院。

sentences.en: He takes to the House floor and he says, quote, no charitable Black scheme can wash out the color of the Negro, can change his inferior nature or save him from his inevitable fate.
sentences.zh: 他在众议院发言时说，引用如下：没有任何慈善性的黑人计划能洗掉黑人的肤色，能改变他低劣的本性，或将他从不可避免的命运中拯救出来。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that this theory of extinction was so mainstream that you could actually hear it being argued on the floor of the house.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，这种灭绝理论在当时已经成为主流，以至于你甚至可以在众议院的辩论中听到它？

sentences.en: Yes, that's correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And so because that theory became so mainstream and so kind of generally accepted, the lack of funding and the lack of resources
sentences.zh: 正因为这一理论变得如此主流，且被普遍接受，导致资金和资源的匮乏

sentences.en: persists and the freedmen hospitals continue to struggle.
sentences.zh: 持续存在，自由民医院也一直举步维艰。

sentences.en: And the ambivalence is so profound that at a freedmen's hospital in North Carolina, when doctors detect smallpox in a couple of their
sentences.zh: 这种冷漠态度非常严重，以至于在北卡罗来纳州的一家自由民医院，当医生在几名

sentences.en: patients, bureau officials are terrified of the disease spreading into the community, but they also don't want to invest the resources to treat it and to prevent that spread.
sentences.zh: 病人身上发现天花时，局里的官员们虽然害怕疾病蔓延到社区，但他们也不愿投入资源去治疗和防止扩散。

sentences.en: So they put out an order to burn their own hospital down.
sentences.zh: 于是他们下令烧毁了自己的医院。

sentences.en: So this is the first example of government funded health care, and it is an example of something that was set up to fail.
sentences.zh: 这是政府资助医疗的第一个例子，也是一个注定要失败的例子。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And, you know, as the hospital burns to the ground, there's this feeling that Black people have that they're on their own, that the
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当医院被烧成平地时，黑人们有一种感觉，那就是他们只能靠自己，

sentences.en: government created this system to help them, but they didn't really want to help them.
sentences.zh: 政府建立这个系统是为了帮助他们，但实际上并不想真正帮助他们。

sentences.en: And so that they were going to have to take care of themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须自力更生。

sentences.en: And Rebecca Lee Crumpler understands this.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡·李·克伦普勒（Rebecca Lee Crumpler）深知这一点。

sentences.en: And she decides to write a book.
sentences.zh: 于是她决定写一本书。

sentences.en: It's called The Book of Medical Discourses in Two Parts.
sentences.zh: 书名是《医学论述两部曲》（The Book of Medical Discourses in Two Parts）。

sentences.en: And it's not addressed to her colleagues in the white medical community or to segregationists in Congress.
sentences.zh: 这本书不是写给白人医学界的同事，也不是写给国会里的种族隔离主义者的。

sentences.en: It's addressed to the Black community, specifically to Black mothers and Black nurses.
sentences.zh: 它是写给黑人社区的，特别是黑人母亲和黑人护士。

sentences.en: And what she tells them in this book is how to take care of themselves, how to prevent diseases like cholera, how to treat basic ailments like hemorrhoids and bronchitis.
sentences.zh: 她在书中告诉她们如何照顾自己，如何预防霍乱等疾病，如何治疗痔疮和支气管炎等基本病症。

sentences.en: And what's so profound about this book is that she's telling Black Americans, you're not inferior.
sentences.zh: 这本书最深刻的地方在于，她告诉非裔美国人：你们并不低劣。

sentences.en: You're not going extinct.
sentences.zh: 你们不会灭绝。

sentences.en: You can take care of yourself.
sentences.zh: 你们可以照顾好自己。

sentences.en: And this is kind of the first example of something that echoes down through the ages, which is Black medical professionals taking matters into their own hands.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是黑人医疗专业人员掌握自己命运的第一个例子，这种精神影响深远，代代相传。

sentences.en: And in the coming decades, they open medical schools, they build hospitals, and they organize themselves to push back against this system that's trying to shut them out completely.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，他们开设医学院，建立医院，并组织起来，共同抵制那个试图将他们完全拒之门外的系统。

sentences.en: Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 总统先生。

sentences.en: So fast forward.
sentences.zh: 让我们快进一下。

sentences.en: Mr. Speaker.
sentences.zh: 议长先生。

sentences.en: To January of 1947.
sentences.zh: 时间来到1947年1月。

sentences.en: Members of the Congress of the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国国会的议员们。

sentences.en: And President Truman's State of the Union address.
sentences.zh: 杜鲁门总统发表国情咨文。

sentences.en: I come before you today to report on the State of the Union.
sentences.zh: 今天我来到这里，向各位报告国情。

sentences.en: It's actually the first State of the Union that's televised.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是第一次通过电视转播的国情咨文。

sentences.en: And he opens with this joke about how both chambers of Congress have been taken over by Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他开场讲了一个笑话，调侃国会两院都被共和党人接管了。

sentences.en: It looks like a good many of you had moved over to the left since I was here laSt.
sentences.zh: 看来我上次来这里之后，你们中有不少人已经转向左翼了。

sentences.en: And so one side of the room is much more full than the other side of the room.
sentences.zh: 所以房间的一侧比另一侧拥挤得多。

sentences.en: And as the New York Times reports, you can clearly see his smile when he makes this joke.
sentences.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，当他讲这个笑话时，可以清楚地看到他的笑容。

sentences.en: A little more than halfway through his speech.
sentences.zh: 在他演讲进行到一半多一点的时候。

sentences.en: Of all our national resources, none is of more basic value than the health of our people.
sentences.zh: 在我们所有的国家资源中，没有什么比我们人民的健康更具基本价值了。

sentences.en: He turns to health care.
sentences.zh: 他转向了医疗保健话题。

sentences.en: Over a year ago, I presented to the Congress my views on a national health program to provide adequate medical care to all who need it.
sentences.zh: 一年多前，我向国会提出了我对国家医疗计划的看法，旨在为所有需要的人提供充足的医疗护理。

sentences.en: What he wants is a government-run health insurance program that everybody pays into ahead of time and that people can draw from when they need it.
sentences.zh: 他想要的是一种由政府运营的医疗保险计划，每个人提前缴费，需要时可以从中支取。

sentences.en: Not as charity, but on the basis of payments made by the beneficiaries of the program.
sentences.zh: 这不是慈善，而是基于计划受益人的缴费。

sentences.en: What he's essentially talking about is universal health care.
sentences.zh: 他本质上谈论的是全民医疗保健。

sentences.en: So by the time Truman's giving this address, the nation's health care system has grown up a bit from the days right after the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 所以当杜鲁门发表这篇演讲时，国家的医疗保健系统已经比内战刚结束时有所发展。

sentences.en: But not by much.
sentences.zh: 但进步并不大。

sentences.en: All of the hospitals that were created through the Freedmen's Bureau have been closed down, except for one that's in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 通过自由民局建立的所有医院都已关闭，只剩下华盛顿特区的一家。

sentences.en: And other hospitals have been built, but there's not nearly enough of them, especially in the South.
sentences.zh: 虽然也建了其他医院，但数量远远不够，尤其是在南方。

sentences.en: And to make matters worse, the hospitals that do exist are all segregated.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，现有的医院都是种族隔离的。

sentences.en: In fact, a separate but equal clause had actually been written into the law.
sentences.zh: 事实上，法律中甚至还写进了“隔离但平等”的条款。

sentences.en: And what that meant was Black patients had to either go to their own Black facilities, which were few and far between in a lot of places,
sentences.zh: 这意味着黑人病人要么必须去他们自己的黑人设施——在很多地方这些设施寥寥无几，

sentences.en: or they were relegated to the basement wards of white hospitals.
sentences.zh: 要么就被安置在白人医院的地下室病房里。

sentences.en: And those wards were small and they did not provide as good care as you got in the white facilities.
sentences.zh: 那些病房很小，提供的护理质量也不如白人设施。

sentences.en: And there were also lots of rules about who white nurses could serve in these hospitals,
sentences.zh: 而且关于白人护士在这些医院里能为谁服务，也有很多规定，

sentences.en: because I know I've read Jim Crow laws that said white nurses couldn't serve Black patients, particularly Black men.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道我读过吉姆·克劳法，上面说白人护士不能为黑人病人服务，特别是黑人男性。

sentences.en: And this is also true for doctors, right?
sentences.zh: 医生也是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, for nurses specifically, because there was a lot of concerns about keeping white women away from Black men.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是护士，因为当时非常担心让白人女性接触黑人男性。

sentences.en: So you maybe had a couple white doctors that would check on Black patients.
sentences.zh: 所以可能只有几个白人医生会查看黑人病人。

sentences.en: But again, even the white doctors that would attend the Black patients would do that after they took care of all of their white patients.
sentences.zh: 但同样，即使是那些会看护黑人病人的白人医生，也是在照顾完所有白人病人之后才会去。

sentences.en: So it was second class in every conceivable way.
sentences.zh: 所以这在各个方面都是二等公民待遇。

sentences.en: But it's not just Black Americans who are not getting enough care.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是非裔美国人得不到足够的护理。

sentences.en: It's many poor white Americans as well.
sentences.zh: 许多贫穷的白人美国人也是如此。

sentences.en: So at that time, most Americans were not insured.
sentences.zh: 当时，大多数美国人都没有保险。

sentences.en: And the insurance that did exist was employer-based, which means you had to get a certain type of job where the employer actually offered this benefit and then you could have it.
sentences.zh: 而现有的保险是基于雇主的，这意味着你必须找到某种工作，雇主确实提供了这项福利，你才能拥有它。

sentences.en: But the problem for Black people and for poor white people is that they didn't have those kinds of jobs that offered health insurance.
sentences.zh: 但黑人和贫穷白人的问题在于，他们没有那种提供医疗保险的工作。

sentences.en: So they had to pay out of pocket.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须自掏腰包。

sentences.en: Basically, the whole system is not working.
sentences.zh: 基本上，整个系统都行不通。

sentences.en: And Truman sees this as one of the most pressing problems the country is facing.
sentences.zh: 杜鲁门认为这是国家面临的最紧迫的问题之一。

sentences.en: And so he decides that national health insurance is the fix.
sentences.zh: 因此他决定，国民健康保险是解决办法。

sentences.en: I've repeatedly asked the Congress to pass a health program.
sentences.zh: 我曾多次要求国会通过一项医疗计划。

sentences.en: And this government-sponsored health insurance initially has really widespread support.
sentences.zh: 这种政府资助的医疗保险最初确实得到了广泛支持。

sentences.en: The nation suffers from lack of medical care.
sentences.zh: 国家正遭受医疗护理匮乏之苦。

sentences.en: That situation can be remedied.
sentences.zh: 这种情况是可以补救的。

sentences.en: But then, days after Truman wins the election, the American Medical Association,
sentences.zh: 但就在杜鲁门赢得选举几天后，美国医学会（AMA），

sentences.en: which is the largest and arguably the most powerful professional organization for doctors in the country, launches this massive campaign to take it down.
sentences.zh: 也就是全国最大、可以说也是最有权势的医生专业组织，发起了一场大规模的运动来推翻它。

sentences.en: And what you have to understand about the AMA is that it's an almost exclusively white organization at that time.
sentences.zh: 你必须了解的是，当时的美国医学会几乎是一个纯白人的组织。

sentences.en: Virtually all of its local chapters exclude Black doctors completely.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的当地分会都完全排斥黑人医生。

sentences.en: And just a few years earlier, the organization had refused to protest the separate-but-equal clause that legalized hospital segregation.
sentences.zh: 就在几年前，该组织还拒绝抗议使医院种族隔离合法化的“隔离但平等”条款。

sentences.en: Plus, this is a time when health care costs are rising and private insurance is really taking off.
sentences.zh: 此外，当时医疗成本正在上升，私人保险正在迅速兴起。

sentences.en: And what the AMA understands is that a national health insurance program is probably going to hurt their profits.
sentences.zh: 美国医学会明白，国民健康保险计划很可能会损害他们的利润。

sentences.en: And so they've actually been fighting against this idea for years.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上多年来一直都在反对这个想法。

sentences.en: And now, with Truman's national health insurance program, they take that fight to a whole new level.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着杜鲁门的国民健康保险计划出台，他们将这场斗争提升到了一个全新的高度。

sentences.en: They've hired a PR firm.
sentences.zh: 他们聘请了一家公关公司。

sentences.en: It's actually the first political consulting firm in the country.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是全国第一家政治咨询公司。

sentences.en: And together, they devised this plan to completely torpedo universal health care.
sentences.zh: 他们共同制定了这个彻底摧毁全民医疗保健的计划。

sentences.en: And what does that fight look like?
sentences.zh: 那场斗争是什么样的？

sentences.en: What it looks like is all-out war.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像一场全面战争。

sentences.en: It's radio ads.
sentences.zh: 有广播广告。

sentences.en: It's newspaper ads.
sentences.zh: 有报纸广告。

sentences.en: It's magazine ads.
sentences.zh: 有杂志广告。

sentences.en: They're delivering pamphlets and mailers to people's homes.
sentences.zh: 他们向人们家中投递小册子和宣传单。

sentences.en: In the end, they send some hundred million pieces of literature all across the country.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们在全国范围内发送了大约一亿份宣传材料。

sentences.en: And what's on that literature and what's in those ads is a campaign slogan.
sentences.zh: 那些材料和广告上的核心是一个竞选口号。

sentences.en: It says, keep politics out of medicine.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：让政治远离医学。

sentences.en: They call Truman's plan socialized medicine.
sentences.zh: 他们称杜鲁门的计划为“社会化医疗”。

sentences.en: They label Truman as a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 他们给杜鲁门贴上了共产主义者的标签。

sentences.en: And you have to remember, this is during a time when communism was a real scare.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，当时正处于人们对共产主义感到极度恐慌的时期。

sentences.en: And they terrify people with this idea that if Truman gets his way, government officials are then going to be able to intervene in private medical decisions.
sentences.zh: 他们用这种想法恐吓人们：如果杜鲁门得逞，政府官员以后就能干预私人医疗决策。

sentences.en: And when they do, they're going to destroy the sacred doctor-patient relationship.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们这样做，就会破坏神圣的医患关系。

sentences.en: And that campaign works.
sentences.zh: 那场运动奏效了。

sentences.en: Popular support for the bill suddenly plummets.
sentences.zh: 公众对该法案的支持率突然暴跌。

sentences.en: It fails to get through Congress.
sentences.zh: 它没能通过国会。

sentences.en: And the health care system that the nation is left with at the end of this fight is still too expensive for most Americans to afford.
sentences.zh: 在这场斗争结束后，国家留下的医疗保健系统对于大多数美国人来说仍然过于昂贵，无法负担。

sentences.en: And as segregated as it has ever been.
sentences.zh: 而且种族隔离程度依然如故。

sentences.en: To Kill a Mockingbird is the most successful American play in Broadway history, says 60 Minutes.
sentences.zh: 《60分钟》节目称，《杀死一只知更鸟》是百老汇历史上最成功的美国戏剧。

sentences.en: Rolling Stone gives it five stars, calling it a landmark production of an American classic.
sentences.zh: 《滚石》杂志给了它五星好评，称其为美国经典的里程碑式制作。

sentences.en: To Kill a Mockingbird is all rise.
sentences.zh: 《杀死一只知更鸟》全场起立致敬。

sentences.en: One of the greatest plays in history raves NPR.
sentences.zh: 美国国家公共电台（NPR）盛赞它是史上最伟大的戏剧之一。

sentences.en: The New York Post says it will change how you see the world.
sentences.zh: 《纽约邮报》称它将改变你看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: This is what great theater is for.
sentences.zh: 这就是伟大戏剧的意义所在。

sentences.en: All rise for Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird, a new play by Aaron Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 为哈珀·李的《杀死一只知更鸟》起立致敬，这是阿伦·索尔金改编的新剧。

sentences.en: This is a phenomenon, says New York Magazine.
sentences.zh: 《纽约杂志》称这是一个现象级作品。

sentences.en: On Broadway at the Schubert Theater.
sentences.zh: 正在百老汇舒伯特剧院上演。

sentences.en: Get tickets at telecharge.com.
sentences.zh: Get tickets at telecharge.com.

sentences.en: Janine, when did all of this start to change?
sentences.zh: 珍妮，这一切是从什么时候开始改变的？

sentences.en: So it really starts to change with a man named Montague Cobb.
sentences.zh: 这确实是从一个名叫蒙塔古·科布（Montague Cobb）的人开始改变的。

sentences.en: Montague Cobb is this fascinating character.
sentences.zh: 蒙塔古·科布是一个迷人的人物。

sentences.en: He's a beloved doctor and medical professor at one of the only black medical colleges in the country at that time, Howard University.
sentences.zh: 他是当时全国仅有的几所黑人医学院之一——霍华德大学的一位深受爱戴的医生和医学教授。

sentences.en: Over 41 years, he teaches thousands of medical students about anatomy.
sentences.zh: 在41年的时间里，他教导了成千上万的医学生解剖学知识。

sentences.en: And he's kind of famous for playing classical music on his violin and reciting poetry for his students while they're dissecting cadavers.
sentences.zh: 他很有名，因为他会在学生解剖尸体时，用小提琴演奏古典音乐并为他们朗诵诗歌。

sentences.en: He's already established himself on the national stage.
sentences.zh: 他已经在全国舞台上确立了自己的地位。

sentences.en: During the fight between Truman and the American Medical Association, Cobb was one of the only doctors to defend Truman's plan and defy the AMA.
sentences.zh: 在杜鲁门与美国医学会的斗争中，科布是仅有的几位捍卫杜鲁门计划并公然反抗美国医学会的医生之一。

sentences.en: Three commissioners said that he had no objection to having colored interns at Gallinger as soon as he could build separate facilities for them.
sentences.zh: 三位专员表示，只要能为黑人实习生建立独立的设施，他不反对在加林格医院接收他们。

sentences.en: Well, that was a bad thing to say at that time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在当时说这种话是很糟糕的。

sentences.en: You know, there's not a lot of recordings of Cobb out there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，关于科布的录音资料并不多。

sentences.en: But there is a documentary from the 1980s called Step by Step, where Cobb himself talks about this time.
sentences.zh: 但有一部20世纪80年代的纪录片叫《一步一个脚印》（Step by Step），科布本人在片中谈到了那个时期。

sentences.en: Steps were also being taken by Dr. Cobb to end segregation in the medical profession.
sentences.zh: 科布医生也正在采取措施结束医疗行业的种族隔离。

sentences.en: I think our first point of overt attack was on the theme of old clothes to Sam, the Negro's hospital dilemma.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们第一次公开攻击的切入点是关于“给黑人的旧衣服”这一主题，即黑人的医院困境。

sentences.en: Cobb used the analogy of whites giving hand-me-down clothes to blacks to illustrate how they also gave blacks hand-me-down hospitals.
sentences.zh: 科布用白人把旧衣服送给黑人的类比，来说明他们是如何把旧医院也送给黑人的。

sentences.en: This one isn't new, but it's better than anything he has or could get.
sentences.zh: 这件虽然不是新的，但比他现在有的或能得到的任何东西都要好。

sentences.en: He's also been outspoken about hospital segregation for years because he recognized how deadly it could be.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直直言不讳地反对医院种族隔离，因为他认识到这可能是致命的。

sentences.en: There's all these horror stories.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的恐怖故事。

sentences.en: They're true stories of black Americans who are mistreated or denied care at white hospitals and die as a result.
sentences.zh: 这些都是真实的非裔美国人的故事，他们在白人医院受到虐待或被拒绝治疗，最终因此死亡。

sentences.en: There's this one example from 1931, where a light-skinned black man gets into a car accident and he's taken to a white hospital.
sentences.zh: 有一个1931年的例子，一个肤色较浅的黑人男子遭遇车祸，被送往一家白人医院。

sentences.en: It's Grady Memorial Hospital.
sentences.zh: 那是格雷迪纪念医院（Grady Memorial Hospital）。

sentences.en: This is in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 这在亚特兰大。

sentences.en: And doctors there, they mistake him for a white patient, so they start treating him.
sentences.zh: 那里的医生误以为他是白人病人，所以开始对他进行治疗。

sentences.en: And it's only when his family comes to the hospital that they realize he's actually black.
sentences.zh: 直到他的家人来到医院，他们才意识到他其实是黑人。

sentences.en: So what do they do?
sentences.zh: 那么他们做了什么？

sentences.en: They pull him off the examining table and they send him to the black ward across the street, where he later dies.
sentences.zh: 他们把他从检查台上拉下来，送到了街对面的黑人病房，他后来在那里去世了。

sentences.en: So these kinds of stories were common knowledge.
sentences.zh: 所以这类故事在当时是众所周知的。

sentences.en: And Montague Cobb really wanted to change that.
sentences.zh: 蒙塔古·科布非常想改变这种状况。

sentences.en: So he launches a national conference on hospital desegregation, and he pulls people in from all over the country to come and talk about this issue every year.
sentences.zh: 于是他发起了一场关于医院废除种族隔离的全国性会议，每年都会召集全国各地的人来讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: And he really implores his white colleagues to take the matter seriously and to think about it.
sentences.zh: 他真诚地恳求他的白人同事们认真对待这件事，并对此进行思考。

sentences.en: But he didn't get very far.
sentences.zh: 但他没能走多远。

sentences.en: Even with all of those efforts, not much changed.
sentences.zh: 即便付出了所有这些努力，情况也没有太大改变。

sentences.en: And he realized eventually that, left to their own devices, white hospitals are going to stay white.
sentences.zh: 他最终意识到，如果任其自然，白人医院只会保持白人专属。

sentences.en: Then, in 1963, he takes the reins of the nation's leading black medical organization.
sentences.zh: 随后，在1963年，他接管了全国领先的黑人医疗组织。

sentences.en: Because remember, the AMA has this history of excluding black doctors.
sentences.zh: 因为请记住，美国医学会（AMA）有着排斥黑人医生的历史。

sentences.en: So what black doctors have had to do is create their own professional societies.
sentences.zh: 所以黑人医生不得不创建自己的专业协会。

sentences.en: And the leading one is called the National Medical Association, or the NMA.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的一个叫作全国医学协会，简称NMA。

sentences.en: And it's at this moment, when Cobb is in this leadership position, that the fight for universal health insurance that started decades back,
sentences.zh: 正是在这一刻，当科布处于领导地位时，几十年前就开始的争取全民医疗保险的斗争，

sentences.en: and the fight for a desegregated health care system that started at the end of the Civil War, finally merge into one fight.
sentences.zh: 以及自内战结束以来就开始的争取废除医疗种族隔离制度的斗争，终于合二为一。

sentences.en: And that fight is about Medicare.
sentences.zh: 而那场斗争就是关于联邦医疗保险（Medicare）。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, the President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们，美国总统。

sentences.en: My fellow Americans, we have had many hard-fought presidential campaigns.
sentences.zh: 我的美国同胞们，我们经历过许多艰难的总统竞选。

sentences.en: So what was the role of Medicare in all of this?
sentences.zh: 那么，联邦医疗保险在这一切中扮演了什么角色呢？

sentences.en: Well, the proposal for Medicare is actually born from the ashes of Truman's failed national health insurance program.
sentences.zh: 嗯，联邦医疗保险的提案实际上诞生于杜鲁门失败的国民健康保险计划的废墟之上。

sentences.en: I intend to preserve and strengthen our social security system.
sentences.zh: 我打算维护并加强我们的社会保障体系。

sentences.en: After that plan dies in Congress, people who want something like it conclude that they need to think smaller and more incrementally.
sentences.zh: 在该计划在国会夭折后，那些想要类似方案的人得出结论，他们需要考虑更小、更渐进的步骤。

sentences.en: I intend to make it stronger by keeping benefits up with rising...
sentences.zh: 我打算通过保持福利水平与不断上涨的……来使其更加强大。

sentences.en: So, beginning under President Kennedy and continuing under President Johnson, their efforts target what is perhaps the most uncontroversial group anyone can think of.
sentences.zh: 因此，从肯尼迪总统任期开始，并延续到约翰逊总统任期，他们的努力目标是人们能想到的最无可争议的群体。

sentences.en: I do not believe that older Americans should be forced to live out their lives in poverty.
sentences.zh: 我不认为美国老年人应该被迫在贫困中度过余生。

sentences.en: Old people.
sentences.zh: 老年人。

sentences.en: Their tiny savings destroyed by illness, dependent upon their relatives, feeling unwanted by their country.
sentences.zh: 他们微薄的积蓄被疾病摧毁，依赖亲戚，感到被国家所抛弃。

sentences.en: The choice is yours.
sentences.zh: 选择权在你们手中。

sentences.en: And once again...
sentences.zh: 再一次……

sentences.en: This bill would put the government smack into your hospital, defining services, setting standards...
sentences.zh: 这项法案将使政府直接介入你们的医院，定义服务，设定标准……

sentences.en: The AMA comes out in full force against the idea.
sentences.zh: 美国医学会全力反对这一想法。

sentences.en: Whether they need it or not, whether they want it or not, they'd be in.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否需要，无论他们是否想要，他们都将被卷入其中。

sentences.en: They use all the same tactics and all the same arguments that they used last time around.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了与上次完全相同的策略和论点。

sentences.en: The American taxpayer certainly has a right to question the free ride.
sentences.zh: 美国纳税人当然有权质疑这种“免费午餐”。

sentences.en: Those who do not need these benefits would be taking at the expense of his children.
sentences.zh: 那些不需要这些福利的人，将以牺牲其子女的利益为代价来承担。

sentences.en: To convince the American public that this is a terrible idea and that it's going to destroy health care as they know it.
sentences.zh: 为了让美国公众相信这是一个糟糕的主意，并且它会摧毁他们所熟知的医疗保健体系。

sentences.en: To the millions of Americans who may have a doubt, I implore you, ask your doctor.
sentences.zh: 对于数百万心存疑虑的美国人，我恳求你们，去问问你们的医生。

sentences.en: Ask your doctor.
sentences.zh: 去问问你们的医生。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: But this time, under Montague Cubs' leadership, the nation's black doctors come out in full force to support Medicare.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，在蒙塔古·科布的领导下，全国的黑人医生全力支持联邦医疗保险。

sentences.en: I decided that all this was bad and I picked up a baseball bat and began to swing it about.
sentences.zh: 我决定这一切都很糟糕，于是我拿起一根棒球棍开始挥舞。

sentences.en: Get a little room.
sentences.zh: 腾出点空间。

sentences.en: They lead protests, they lobby Congress, and they launch their own public relations campaign, explaining to the nation that, in fact, this won't destroy medicine.
sentences.zh: 他们领导抗议，游说国会，并开展了自己的公关活动，向全国解释说，事实上，这不会摧毁医学。

sentences.en: This will make medicine more equitable.
sentences.zh: 这将使医学更加公平。

sentences.en: And their message is what it's been for a long time.
sentences.zh: 他们的信息与长期以来的一样。

sentences.en: Health care is a human right.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健是一项基本人权。

sentences.en: And that any program that expands access to health care is the duty of a free and democratic society.
sentences.zh: 任何扩大医疗保健获取渠道的计划都是自由民主社会的责任。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the fight for civil rights is escalating all across the country, outside of the medical world.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在医疗界之外，全国各地的民权斗争正在升级。

sentences.en: This Civil Rights Act is a challenge to all of us.
sentences.zh: 这部《民权法案》是对我们所有人的挑战。

sentences.en: And, of course, that effort culminates in the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which says that discriminating on the basis of race is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 当然，这一努力最终促成了1964年的《民权法案》，该法案规定基于种族的歧视是违宪的。

sentences.en: The last vestiges of injustice.
sentences.zh: 不公正的最后残余。

sentences.en: And more specifically, it says that the government can pull federal dollars from any facility or entity that does not comply with the law.
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，它规定政府可以从任何不遵守法律的机构或实体中撤回联邦资金。

sentences.en: And that includes hospitals.
sentences.zh: 这其中就包括医院。

sentences.en: We must not approach the observance and enforcement of this law in a vengeful spirit.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不能以复仇的心态来对待这部法律的遵守和执行。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of hospitals do nothing.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数医院什么也没做。

sentences.en: They don't just suddenly desegregate.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有突然废除种族隔离。

sentences.en: And it's unclear when or even if they're going to face any consequences at all for that.
sentences.zh: 而且尚不清楚他们何时，甚至是否会因此面临任何后果。

sentences.en: And this is where Medicare comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是联邦医疗保险发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: Because Medicare is like a new pile of federal money that's dangled in front of hospitals across the country.
sentences.zh: 因为联邦医疗保险就像一堆新的联邦资金，悬在全国各地的医院面前。

sentences.en: But in order to get that money, hospitals have to comply with federal law, like the Civil Rights Act.
sentences.zh: 但为了获得这笔钱，医院必须遵守联邦法律，比如《民权法案》。

sentences.en: They would have to actually desegregate.
sentences.zh: 他们必须真正废除种族隔离。

sentences.en: So, as Congress begins to debate the bill, Montague Cobb knows that this is the moment to both create a national health insurance program and desegregate the nation's hospitals.
sentences.zh: 因此，当国会开始辩论该法案时，蒙塔古·科布知道，这是既能建立国民健康保险计划，又能废除全国医院种族隔离的关键时刻。

sentences.en: And when he's called upon to testify, he says that after two decades of arguing and equivocating,
sentences.zh: 当他被传唤作证时，他说，经过二十年的争论和推诿，

sentences.en: it is past time for the nation's leaders to take, quote, definitive action to expand access to health care.
sentences.zh: 国家领导人采取所谓“决定性行动”以扩大医疗保健获取渠道的时机早已成熟。

sentences.en: And at the end of his testimony, he recites this hymn by Charles Matheson.
sentences.zh: 在证词的最后，他背诵了查尔斯·马西森的这首赞美诗。

sentences.en: And it goes,
sentences.zh: 它是这样写的：

sentences.en: Oh, love that will not let me go, I hide my helpless self in thee.
sentences.zh: 哦，那永不放手的爱，我将无助的自己藏于你怀中。

sentences.en: I give thee back the life I owe, that in thine ocean depths its flow may richer, fuller be.
sentences.zh: 我将我所欠的生命归还于你，愿它在你深邃的海洋中，变得更加丰富、更加充盈。

sentences.en: And then he tells Congress,
sentences.zh: 然后他告诉国会：

sentences.en: Like this love, the benefits of Medicare cannot be taken away.
sentences.zh: 就像这份爱一样，联邦医疗保险的福利是无法被剥夺的。

sentences.en: And he asks them,
sentences.zh: 他问他们：

sentences.en: Can we deny this small assurance to those on whose shoulders we stand?
sentences.zh: 我们能否拒绝给予那些我们站在其肩膀上的人这一小小的保障？

sentences.en: So I'm willing to struggle along and let us learn step by step.
sentences.zh: 所以我愿意努力前行，让我们一步一步地学习。

sentences.en: But because man is such a slow learner, let us recognize our mistakes.
sentences.zh: 但因为人类是一个学习缓慢的物种，让我们认识到自己的错误。

sentences.en: And remedy them without having to repeat the historical process again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 并纠正它们，而不必一次又一次地重复历史进程。

sentences.en: And so Medicare passes.
sentences.zh: 于是，联邦医疗保险法案通过了。

sentences.en: And what happens is, within four months of implementation, nearly 3,000 hospitals desegregate.
sentences.zh: 结果是，在实施后的四个月内，近3000家医院废除了种族隔离。

sentences.en: But of course, the health disparities between Black Americans and white Americans persist to this day.
sentences.zh: 但当然，黑人与白人之间的健康差距至今仍然存在。

sentences.en: Black women are three times more likely to die of causes related to pregnancy than white women.
sentences.zh: 黑人女性因怀孕相关原因死亡的可能性是白人女性的三倍。

sentences.en: Black people with HIV tend to get worse care than white people with a disease.
sentences.zh: 患有艾滋病的黑人得到的护理往往比患有该病的白人更差。

sentences.en: One study found that Black patients with diabetes did worse than white patients, even when they had the same doctor.
sentences.zh: 一项研究发现，即使拥有相同的医生，患有糖尿病的黑人患者的治疗效果也比白人患者差。

sentences.en: Black Americans die at higher rates from many cancers that would have been treatable had they been caught earlier.
sentences.zh: 许多如果及早发现本可治疗的癌症，黑人患者的死亡率却更高。

sentences.en: My name is Yaa Gyasi, and I'm going to read a short piece I wrote called Bad Blood.
sentences.zh: 我叫亚·加西，我将朗读我写的一篇短文，题为《坏血》。

sentences.en: Upon closer inspection, the leaf her two-year-old was attempting to put in his mouth in the middle of the playground on that lovely fall day was in fact a used tampon.
sentences.zh: 仔细一看，那个秋日里，她两岁的孩子在操场中央试图放进嘴里的叶子，实际上是一个用过的卫生棉条。

sentences.en: She snatched it from him and Purelled both of their hands before rushing them back to their apartment on Dean.
sentences.zh: 她从他手中夺过它，给他们俩的手都用了免洗洗手液，然后匆忙带他们回到了迪恩街的公寓。

sentences.en: She put him in the bath and scrubbed, and by the time her husband found them, they were both crying.
sentences.zh: 她让他洗了个澡，用力擦洗，当她丈夫找到他们时，他们都在哭。

sentences.en: We have to leave New York, she said, after he'd put the baby to bed.
sentences.zh: “我们必须离开纽约，”她在丈夫哄孩子上床睡觉后说道。

sentences.en: Let's move back home.
sentences.zh: “我们搬回老家吧。”

sentences.en: There are tampons in Alabama, he said.
sentences.zh: “阿拉巴马州也有卫生棉条，”他说。

sentences.en: And then, what's the worst that could happen?
sentences.zh: 那么，最坏的情况会是什么呢？

sentences.en: It was the question they'd played out since graduate school, when her hypochondria had been all-consuming.
sentences.zh: 这是他们从研究生院起就一直在脑海中演练的问题，那时她的疑病症已经到了令人窒息的地步。

sentences.en: Back then, leaning into her fears, describing them, had given her some comfort.
sentences.zh: 那时，沉溺于恐惧并描述它们，曾给她带来一些安慰。

sentences.en: But then they had Booker, and suddenly, the worst looked so much worse.
sentences.zh: 但后来他们有了布克，突然间，最坏的情况看起来变得更糟了。

sentences.en: He could get an STD, and then we'd be the Black parents at the hospital with a baby with an STD,
sentences.zh: “他可能会得性病，然后我们就会成为医院里带着患性病婴儿的黑人父母，

sentences.en: and the pediatrician would call social services, and they would take him away, and we'd end up in jail.
sentences.zh: 儿科医生会打电话给社会服务机构，他们会把他带走，我们最终会进监狱。”

sentences.en: Okay, he said slowly.
sentences.zh: “好吧，”他慢慢地说。

sentences.en: That would be bad, but it's statistically very, very unlikely.
sentences.zh: “那会很糟糕，但在统计学上是非常、非常不可能发生的。”

sentences.en: Would it make you feel better if we called the doctor?
sentences.zh: “如果我们给医生打电话，你会感觉好点吗？”

sentences.en: She shook her head.
sentences.zh: 她摇了摇头。

sentences.en: Her husband only used the word statistically when he wanted to avoid using the words, you're crazy.
sentences.zh: 她丈夫只有在想避免说出“你疯了”这几个字时，才会使用“在统计学上”这个词。

sentences.en: She knew that the doctor would just tell her to trust him.
sentences.zh: 她知道医生只会告诉她要信任他。

sentences.en: But she also knew that when the worst happens in this country, it often happens to them.
sentences.zh: 但她也知道，当最坏的情况发生在这个国家时，它往往发生在他们身上。

sentences.en: She comes by her hypochondria and iatrophobia honestly.
sentences.zh: 她的疑病症和对医生的恐惧并非空穴来风。

sentences.en: When she was growing up in Alabama, people still talked about their grandfathers, fathers, and brothers who had died of bad blood.
sentences.zh: 当她在阿拉巴马州长大时，人们还在谈论他们死于“坏血病”的祖父、父亲和兄弟。

sentences.en: That was the catch-all term for syphilis, anemia, and just about anything that ailed you.
sentences.zh: 那是梅毒、贫血以及几乎所有折磨你的疾病的统称。

sentences.en: The 600 Black men who were enrolled in the Tuskegee study were told they'd get free medical care.
sentences.zh: 参加塔斯基吉研究的600名黑人男子被告知他们将获得免费医疗。

sentences.en: Instead, from 1932 to 1972, researchers with the United States Public Health Service watched as the men developed lesions on their mouths and genitals.
sentences.zh: 然而，从1932年到1972年，美国公共卫生局的研究人员眼睁睁地看着这些男人的口腔和生殖器长出病变。

sentences.en: Watched as their lymph nodes swelled, as their hair fell out.
sentences.zh: 看着他们的淋巴结肿大，看着他们的头发脱落。

sentences.en: Watched as the disease moved into its final stages, leaving the men blind and demented.
sentences.zh: 看着疾病进入最后阶段，使这些人失明并患上痴呆症。

sentences.en: Leaving them to die.
sentences.zh: 任由他们死去。

sentences.en: All this when they knew a simple penicillin shot would cure them.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生时，他们明明知道一针青霉素就能治愈他们。

sentences.en: All this because they wanted to see what would happen.
sentences.zh: 这一切仅仅是因为他们想看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: For years afterward, her grandmother refused to go to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 此后的多年里，她的祖母拒绝去医院。

sentences.en: Even at 89, perpetually hunched over in the throes of an endless cough, she'd repeat, anything but the doctor.
sentences.zh: 即使在89岁时，她因无休止的咳嗽而终日佝偻着背，她仍会重复说：“什么都行，就是别找医生。”

sentences.en: Bad blood begets bad blood.
sentences.zh: 坏血滋生坏血。

sentences.en: She's more trusting than her grandmother, but she still has her moments.
sentences.zh: 她比她的祖母更信任医生，但她仍然会有动摇的时刻。

sentences.en: Like many women, she was nervous about giving birth.
sentences.zh: 像许多女性一样，她对分娩感到紧张。

sentences.en: All the more so because she was doing it in New York City, where Black women are 12 times more likely to die in childbirth than white women.
sentences.zh: 更何况她是在纽约市分娩，在那里，黑人女性死于分娩的可能性是白人女性的12倍。

sentences.en: And in that very statistic, the indelible impression of Tuskegee, the lingering, niggling feeling that they are never fully safe in a country
sentences.zh: 正是这一统计数据，留下了塔斯基吉事件不可磨灭的印记，那种挥之不去的、细微的恐惧感——在这个国家，他们永远无法完全安全，

sentences.en: where doctors and researchers had no qualms about watching hundreds of Black men die slowly,
sentences.zh: 在这里，医生和研究人员可以毫无顾忌地看着数百名黑人男子缓慢地、

sentences.zh: 残忍地死去，仅仅因为他们可以这样做。

sentences.en: When she held Booker in her arms for the first time and saw her grandmother's nose on his perfect face, love and fear rose up in her.
sentences.zh: 当她第一次把布克抱在怀里，看到他那张完美的脸上有着她祖母的鼻子时，爱与恐惧在她心中油然而生。

sentences.zh: “最坏的情况会是什么？”她丈夫问，而她无法说出口，那最坏的情况。
